q1_format.2012_13_to_2017_18: 10 teams, 36 rounds, quadruple round-robin (4 meetings per pair, 2 home + 2 away), 180 matches per season, no split, no points halving
q1_format.2018_19_to_2025_26: 12 teams, 32 rounds (regular season Grunddurchgang 22 + final round 10), split after round 22 into Meistergruppe / Qualifikationsgruppe (6 teams each, 10 more rounds, rounds 23-32), 32 matches per team, 192 league matches per season

points_halving.in_force: 2018/19 to 2025/26 (last season); abolished from 2026/27 (full points carried into Finaldurchgang, bundesliga.at 2026/27 Spielbetriebsrichtlinien section 3b)
points_halving.rule: rounded DOWN (abgerundet); a club rounded down ranks ahead on equal points (the half point is the first tiebreak)
points_halving.evidence: bundesliga.at 2025/26 season guide, OFBL 2016 reform details (bundesliga.at 2016-12-02), German Wikipedia 2025/26 Modus section, Sky Sport Austria 2026-05-09, plus empirical 2019/20 cases (Salzburg 48->24, Hartberg 29->14, Austria Wien 25->12); official table footnote on bundesliga.at confirms the half-point rounding-down wording
points_halving.rejected: austriabuliwetten.com and statsultra.com claim rounding UP (45 -> 23); secondary betting-site claims, contradicted by official sources and empirical cases
points_halving.wording_note: The 2014/15 season page literally says each pair met twice (home + away), contradicting the 36-round / 36-matches-per-team / 180-match arithmetic; the 2015/16 page explicitly says twice home and twice away. Ruled 4 meetings per pair on the explicit 2015/16 wording plus six-season arithmetic; the 2014/15 wording is treated as an error / half-season description.

highlights: Salzburg: founded 1933-09-13 as SV Austria Salzburg, first top flight 1953/54; Red Bull takeover 2005-04-06, OFB ordered the 'founded 2005' claim removed; fan-founded SV Austria Salzburg is a separate club
Grazer AK: original entity first top flight 1951/52, dissolved 2012; phoenix entity back in the Bundesliga 2024/25
LASK and Sturm Graz first top-flight seasons in the Gauliga Ostmark era (1940/41 and 1941/42); post-war national-league first seasons 1949/50 for both
WSG Tirol is the Wattens entity (founded 1930, first top flight 1969/70), NOT Wacker Innsbruck; SSW Innsbruck merger titles 1971-84 are not counted for WSG
WAC: independent first top flight 2012/13 (2007-12 cooperation team with St. Andra, separate legal entities)
